header.title: How to Repair a Leaking Coffeemaker
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to diagnose and repair common leaks in a coffeemaker. It covers cleaning, inspecting key components like the pump valve and brew switch, and checking tube connectors.

steps.description: Clean the coffee maker by running a vinegar and water solution through a brewing cycle to dissolve buildup.
actions: Mix 11 cups of white vinegar and 1 cup of fresh water.
Fill the coffee pot to the 11 cup mark with white vinegar.
Fill the coffee pot to the 12 cup mark with fresh water.
Pour the vinegar and water mixture into the reservoir.
Turn on the coffee maker.
Allow the coffee maker to run through a brewing cycle.
Repeat the cleaning cycle if necessary.

steps.description: Inspect the coffee maker's pump valve for damage or clogs, which can prevent water flow and potentially cause leaks.
actions: Unplug the coffee maker
Examine the pump valve
Check for a broken pump valve
Check for a clog in the pump valve
If pump is sealed, replace the whole pump
If pump is not sealed, check for coffee grounds or mineral deposits

steps.description: This step involves testing the brew switch functionality by removing the base plate and using a volt-ohmmeter to check for continuity.
actions: Examine the brewing switch
Remove the base plate
Test the switch with a volt-ohmmeter
Touch the tester to the RX1 scale
Check the reading on the volt-ohmmeter
Replace the switch (if necessary)

steps.description: Inspect the tube connectors for leaks and replace them if necessary to resolve leaking or sputtering issues.
actions: Inspect the tube connectors
Clean the surfaces of an elbow if a leak is found
Replace the tube and elbow if a tube connector leaks
